svg.title: Global Hecke cotangents, compatible Higgs fibres and the curve covector
svg.desc: The gluing tangent maps to b minus a1 plus a2. A one-pole residue theorem proves the global cotangent equality. Regular transformed disc fields glue uniquely on every coefficient test. A central cocharacter with nonzero pairing gives a nonzero moving curve covector, and both bounded compatible Higgs fibres are isolated reduced points.
svg.text: Global Hecke: a residue identity and a moving covector
X smooth connected projective, k algebraically closed of characteristic zero; x ∈ X(k)
α : P₂|U → P₁|U; U = X − {x}; B invariant nondegenerate; u = t − x
1. The actual fixed-point gluing tangent
W = 𝔤((u)), V = Γ(U,E), L₂ = 𝔤[[u]], L₁ = Ad(g⁻¹)𝔤[[u]]
d(U₁,U₂,v₁,v₂) = (U₁ − v₁, U₂ − v₂, U₁ − U₂)
V² ⊕ L₁ ⊕ L₂ → W² ⊕ V, in degrees −1,0 • automorphisms retained
p₁
[a₁]
W / (V + L₁)
rₓ
q = b − a₁ + a₂
W / (L₁ + L₂)
p₂
[a₂]
W / (V + L₂)
HG.1–HG.5 • qd = v₁ − v₂ is exactly the local arc boundary
2. Compatible global fields give the cotangent equality
A₂ = α* A₁ on U; η is their common punctured covector.
Resₓ⟨A,b⟩ = 0: the rational differential has only one possible pole.
p₁*ξ₁ + rₓ*η = p₂*ξ₂; rₓ*η(a₁,a₂,b) = Resₓ⟨A,−a₁+a₂⟩
HG.6–HG.7 • converse: independent a₁ and a₂ tests force the same Laurent field
3. Regular disc fields glue uniquely on every coefficient test
A₂ on U = α*A₁; A₂ on D = Ad(g⁻¹)A(u) du, required regular
Fixed identified input fibre ≃ Spr_(G,A)(R), for every ordinary k-algebra R
Cartier injectivity: f is a nonzerodivisor ⇒ E → E[1/f] is injective.
F(A₁) = F(A₂) for every homogeneous invariant F; nilpotent equations transfer.
HG.8–HG.11 • no reduction of R and no quotient by fixed-input automorphisms
4. The central cocharacter gives the positive curve covector
After Levi normalization: A(u) ∈ 𝔪[[u]], A(0)=C, g=u^λ, B(C,dλ) ≠ 0
crystal lift − coordinate lift = g⁻¹g′; ξₓ = B(C,dλ) dx ≠ 0
p₁*ξ₁ + r*θ = p₂*ξ₂ + s*ξₓ; θ has zero coordinate curve component.
Fixed input, bound at λ
u^λ is open, isolated and reduced.
Fixed output, opposite bound
u^(−λ) is open, isolated and reduced.
SL₃: C = diag(1,1,−2) + E₁₂, λ = (1,1,−2), ω=q(u)du ⇒ ξₓ=6q(0)dx
HG.12–HG.16 and AS.6 • Exercise 3.V assumes q(0) ≠ 0
Satake singular support and survival under proper direct image remain required.
Free further reading: Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Rozenblyum–Varshavsky, arXiv:1908.05420v5, B.6
